newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farmers urge action against EU farm reform.
newsitem.headline: French farmers urge action against EU farm reform.

text.p: Two of France's largest farm unions on Friday called on farmers to mobilise on July 21 to protest against a controversial European Commission plan to cut farm subsidies.
The following day European farm ministers will discuss the Agenda 2000 plan, which aims to prepare the European Union's eastern expansion.

In a joint statement the broad-based FNSEA union and young farmers' union CNJA said their representatives will present the administrative heads of regions and parliamentaries with a motion on Monday, stating their opposition to the plan.
"The FNSEA and CNJA reject the Commission proposals as they stand," FNSEA official Jean Dube told Reuters.
Dube also said that other actions will follow but he did not say what form they might take.
"People are not expected to bring out bulldozers," he added.

In the motion farmers say they oppose the planned farm price reform because it threatens farmers' revenues, jobs and rural development. They also consider it a surrender to American moves towards phasing out subsidies.
The United States last year introduced farm reform to give its farmers a better chance to compete on world markets.

Last Wednesday FNSEA union leader Luc Guyau met Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin to discuss the EU plan. After the meeting he said proposals to cut EU subsidies were "unacceptable" and claimed he had the full support of the government.
France has said the plan, aimed at making EU farmers more competitive by lowering prices toward world levels, would weaken the EU's bargaining power in the next round of global trade talks from 1999.
It also fears that the Commission proposal to shift agriculture support from guaranteed prices and export subsidies to direct payment to farmers might prove costly and disadvantage some sectors.
